frequency_question: How often does comprehensive energy permitting reform pass both houses and get signed into law within a single congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes major bipartisan or party-led energy/permitting reform packages explicitly aimed at streamlining infrastructure or pipeline approvals; excludes minor riders attached to must-pass appropriations unless they constitute comprehensive reform.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007
EPW Permitting Reform Push (Manchin Bill) 117th Congress
Debt Limit Deal Permitting Provisions 118th Congress
Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (118th Congress)

coverage_note: 5 named major legislative cycles; comprehensive reform attempts occur roughly once every three sessions, with historical passage in major omnibus form about 40 percent of the time when prioritized.
known_gaps: Excludes minor administrative rule changes by federal agencies and isolated state-level reforms.
skeleton: 5 distinct major legislative push cycles for energy permitting reform across 15 congressional sessions since 1995 where comprehensive reform was actively attempted.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 5 major structured push cycles equals base rate frequency.
validity_reason: Legislative polarization trends and procedural rules in the Senate remain stable over multi-year horizons, anchoring the base rate.
